findings.reason: a node implementing §17 literally against `RowPolicy._reported` will find the memory run-id-keyed and lift rows carrying none, so the named mechanism is a no-op for the very rows it is meant to hold; the plan must name the lift identity the memory is held under (the lift's group/id), or the node burns a round discovering and re-deciding the key mid-implementation.
findings.text: §17's deliverable names the mechanism "`RowPolicy`'s per-pane `_reported` memory in `reckon/crew/ticker.py` holds a baseline lift row whose lift the pane already drew", but that memory cannot key a lift row: `_reported` is `dict[str, str]` keyed by run id (`reckon/crew/ticker.py:1293`) and `RowPolicy.feed` derives its key as `str(event.get("run_id") or "")` with no node fallback (`reckon/crew/ticker.py:1498`), while a lift row is built with `"run_id": None` (`reckon/crew/lift_watch.py:192`). So for every lift row the key is the empty string, each guarded read/write is skipped (`if run_id` guards at `reckon/crew/ticker.py:1579`), and the row is delivered unconditionally by the `not run_id` fallback (`reckon/crew/ticker.py:1615`, `:1628`) — the policy never remembers and never suppresses a lift row as named. The plan's claim is false of the code it cites. (Contrast the renderer's own grid, which does fall back to the node: `run_id = str(event.get("run_id") or node)` at `reckon/crew/ticker.py:2065`, so the grid keys a lift row by its group — but §17 names the policy's memory, not the grid's.)
